overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law deliberation in the six 2020 emails, relying on OML 2022-31 for four and finding the other two administrative, so no violation and no remedy.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that four of six March-April 2020 Council emails were deliberation outside a posted meeting; the AG relied on OML 2022-31 for these.
allegations.key_passage: On February 28, 2022, in response to a separate Open Meeting Law complaint filed by another complainant, our office issued a determination finding that four of the six emails referenced in the instant complaint did not constitute deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that two further March-April 2020 emails, one forwarding Mayor's office information and one announcing canceled meetings, were deliberation outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we also find that the two additional emails at issue in this complaint—one forwarding information from the Special Assistant to the Mayor and one announcing that meetings had been canceled—did not constitute deliberation for purposes of the Open Meeting Law.
